parameters.identity: Source: the small rigid rectangular package with a pale blue-gray printed top labeled Cream Cheese in white script with dark-blue graphics. It lies broad-face-up on the wooden countertop, left of the bowl in the wrist image and right of the bowl in agentview. Its top and narrow side faces are visible. Destination: the open round bowl with a thin yellowish rim and dense black-and-white floral/geometric interior pattern, between the plate and dark bottle in the wrist image. Its inner lip and cavity bottom are visible.
landmark_definitions: l0: Center of the large white initial C in the printed word Cream on the package top.
l1: Center of the terminal white e in the printed word Cheese on the package top.
l2: Center of the large white initial C in the printed word Cheese, adjacent to the dark-blue oval badge on the package top.

evidence.explanation: The source is the rectangular Cream Cheese package, and the destination is the open patterned bowl. The package has a visible planar printed top and visible narrow right and near side faces extending down to the same wooden countertop, supporting that it rests flat. Its underside is not observed or inferred from a top sample. The bowl has an approximately circular inner rim and a visible cavity bottom; its opening is not visibly obstructed. These observations support the requested object eligibility, not a clearance certificate for a subsequent transport motion. Only frame 0 is available.

evidence.explanation: The proposed high_alignment action is locally supported with the gripper open. This review covers the elevated alignment move only, not descent, closure, transport, or placement. Current and earlier images show the same labeled Cream Cheese package and patterned bowl without visible displacement or evidence of interaction. The proposed pad height is essentially unchanged from the current height. The supplied finger envelope has a lowest world height of approximately 1.161 m, well above the currently visible package top near 0.918 m and bowl lip near 0.947 m. The visible countertop and intervening object surfaces support this elevated local move; no external material is observed obstructing it. The tall cabinet and wooden rack are outside this local approach area. This is positive local support, not a global clearance certificate. The end-biased target is not itself a reason to reject elevated alignment; actual finger lanes and finite pad-side overlap must be assessed for a subsequent descent. The dark robot geometry at the bottom of the wrist image is self-occlusion, not an external obstacle, and does not hide the selected target or bowl surfaces. The bowl prior remains consistent with current observations. Existing landmark names are returned with fresh pixel selections because they remain visible. Regions provide distributed package, bowl, and exposed support measurements; these are visible surfaces only, not inferred hidden geometry.

The proposed open-hand descent to source_hover is locally supported. The cream-cheese label, rectangular top, and placement relative to the bowl and plate agree with the earlier views. The fixed agentview shows no source or bowl displacement; the wrist-image changes are consistent with camera motion. The acknowledged high, open-hand approach shows no evidence of a disturbing interaction, so the saved geometry remains a short-horizon prior, not a fresh measurement.

Current visible tabletop flanks both actual finger lanes near the selected package end. The supplied final finger envelope has a minimum height of about 0.9546 m, approximately 0.036 m above the package top and 0.055 m above its support. The visible package boundary supports the end-biased alignment and finite approximately 0.0135 m longitudinal pad/side overlap; centering along the whole package is unnecessary. This action stops above contact and does not establish a grasp.

No external material is observed obstructing this local descent. The bowl and plate are outside these local finger lanes; a fitted inner-lip proxy is not being treated as occupied material. Relevant source and lane surfaces are observed. The wrist view partially self-occludes the bowl, so k2, k3, and k4 are returned from the unobstructed agentview; the other bowl samples use visible wrist surfaces. Package corner samples are slightly inset onto the top surface to avoid mixed edge depth. These observations do not certify a later descent, closure, transfer corridor, retention, or task completion.

The proposed open-gripper grasp descent is locally supported. The visible Cream Cheese printing, near-end edge and exposed package surface agree with the earlier stationary package in agentview and with the changed wrist-camera viewpoint. No target displacement or inconsistent identity is observed. The recorded open-hand approach and current finger height do not indicate a disturbing interaction.

The actual open finger lanes flank the package width and lead toward visible bare tabletop, not toward the bowl or plate. The supplied geometry supports an end-biased pinch: the approximately 0.0135 m longitudinal pad/side overlap is finite despite the grasp not being centered along the package. At the proposed pad height, the pads overlap the upper package side vertically. The supplied lowest finger height is approximately 0.903 m versus the approximately 0.900 m support plane, giving a small modeled table margin. These observations support only the stated descent with the gripper open and the stated orientation; they do not certify a later corridor, closing outcome or retention.

Some package features and the right part of the bowl are hidden by the robot. This is self-occlusion, not observed external obstructing material. Current measurements are returned for l0, l2, package_top_corner_0, package_top_corner_1, k0 through k3 and floor. l1, package_top_corner_2, package_top_corner_3, k4 and k5 cannot be reliably measured on their physical surfaces in the current views because of robot occlusion; their stationary projections are not substituted for observations. The exposed bowl and source surfaces show no disagreement with the short-horizon prior. The regions provide current package surfaces and the two local finger-lane support patches for geometric checking.

Bracketing is observed. In both current views, actual open finger tips visibly flank opposite sides of the exposed cream cheese package, with gaps between each finger and the package. The earlier images identify the same package; the current hand is lower around it. No table or neighboring object is visibly intruding into these local gaps. The gripper itself occludes lower portions of the wrist view, so this is not a certificate of hidden clearance or evidence of contact, retention, or task completion.
